question: Should OpenClaw core add a native cross-gateway session messaging primitive, and if so should it use gateway.peers-style direct routing or a broader federation/remote-node contract?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses core gateway auth, session state, message delivery, and operator configuration boundaries; source inspection confirms the feature is missing, but the safe API and trust model require maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor core federation design
options.body: Keep this issue open with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87733 as the design track and require auth, identity, delivery, and upgrade proof before landing code.

options.title: Narrow the linked PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/43656 as the implementation candidate after resolving conflicts, upgrade behavior, security review, and real multi-gateway proof.

options.title: Defer to plugin or MCP bridge
options.body: Close or redirect only if maintainers decide core should not own cross-gateway sessions and current plugin/MCP surfaces are sufficient.

recommendation.title: Sponsor core federation design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87733 as the design track and require auth, identity, delivery, and upgrade proof before landing code.

likelyOwner.reason: stainlu is tied to the current issue-routing timeline and is the best available owner for gateway/session architecture direction among the identified candidates.
